literal: Even in ruin there is a benefit: relatives (acc.) having stretched that which measures, a rod.
translation: Even in ruin there is a certain benefit: it acts as a measuring rod to stretch out and measure one's true friends.
modern: ஒருவனுக்கு வரும் துன்பத்திலும் ஒரு நன்மை உண்டு; அத்துன்பமே அவனுடைய நண்பர்களின் உண்மையான இயல்பை அளந்து காட்டும் அளவுகோலாக அமையும்.
explanation: This couplet reveals a hidden advantage in facing adversity. The word 'கேடு' refers to ruin or hardship, while 'உறுதி' means a solid benefit or good. The poet uses the metaphor of a measuring rod ('கோல்') that is stretched out ('நீட்டி') to measure things. Hardship acts exactly like this rod, allowing a person to accurately measure the true loyalty and worth of their friends and relatives ('கிளைஞர்'). Thus, adversity is not entirely bad, as it exposes who one's real companions are.
